newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU must commit to ratify budget pact - economist.
newsitem.headline: EU must commit to ratify budget pact - economist.

text.p: Deutsche Bank AG chief economist Norbert Walter said on Thursday if European Union finance ministers fail to ratify a budgetary discipline pact at next week's Amsterdam summit, they must commit themselves to approving an accord by the autumn.

"It will be very important to have a consensus statement that they will attempt to reach an agreement during the summer and ratify it by the autumn," he told reporters after addressing a seminar on monetary union.
He said it would be important to reassure financial markets the ministers were "building a consensus" on the pact meant to enforce fiscal discipline after introduction of the euro.
"Europe -- France and Germany -- are a crossroads for their future," he said.
France's new Socialist-led government shocked EU members on Monday by asking for a delay in ratifying the stability pact. It has said it wants more stress on growth and employment.
Walter rated chances that monetary union could be derailed at 35 percent. Collapse of the drive to monetary union would lead to speculative attacks against European currencies, he warned.

He said he believes that if the euro were launched, it would likely include Spain, Portugal and perhaps Italy if it could demonstrate it was on course to cut its deficit to three percent of gross domestic product, as required by the Maastricht treaty.
But Italy would have to take measures to reform its pension system to be part of the first wave in order to show that its deficit improvement was sustainable.
A wider euro would likely be a weaker currency but that would help drive exports and boost European economies, he said.
